answer.rationale: p99 latency spike of 5x target coinciding with a release 2 hours ago is the strongest temporal signal. memory_b1 demonstrates that rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact and is faster than alternatives. memory_b2 shows regional failover carries write-loss risk during heavy settlement traffic—exactly our current condition—making it dangerous. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) help contain failures but don't address root cause if the release is faulty. Capacity and read-replica routing don't address a bad build. Verification of b1 confirms rollback speed and safety precedent; verification of b2 confirms the write-loss risk that rules out failover. Rolling back first is the lowest-risk intervention that preserves writes and can be executed during the settlement peak. If rollback succeeds, latency pressure drops and we can evaluate other actions. If it fails or latency persists post-rollback, the root cause is not the release, and we can then pursue capacity or circuit-breaker measures.
